messages:
alex: FYI support escalated a performance regression for customer Maple (dedicated, us-west-2). They see ~2x p50 and ~30% throughput drop since last night on redwood-v2-small. Attaching sample request ids. Can runtime team pick this up? :eyes:

mike: Got it. Any spike in traffic or config changes on their Dedicated pool?

support-bot: customer_report: Maple #INC-2026 attached logs and sample req ids: req=aa12bb, aa12bc, aa12bd. Noted start ~2026-03-16T22:10Z.

priya: @mike I checked provisioning events — no recent instance type changes. Autoscaler did add 1 node at 22:12 but that should lower latency not increase it.

olivia: I pulled the logs, see an increase in KV cache miss rate for that model around the same time. Could be cold cache or eviction storm. sample from logs:

```
kvcache: miss rate 0.48 -> 0.72
serving: p50 34ms -> 78ms
throughput(rps) 1200 -> 840
```

sam: Interesting. If KV cache misses spiked, per-token runtime becomes 2-3x. Steps: 1) reproduce locally with bench, 2) collect profile on service (nvprof/traces), 3) check routing fallback to larger model variant. I'll take step 1.

bench-bot: starting benchmark: ./tools/bench --model redwood-v2-small --seq 512 --concurrency 8 --region us-west-2 --sample-req aa12bb --profile out/bench-aa12bb.prof

alex: Thanks. Also check prefix cache warmup — customer uses long chat sessions with repeated context reuse. Might interact with cache eviction when autoscaler resizes pools.

mike: Reproduced locally — baseline (yesterday snapshot) p50 ~36ms, throughput ~1150 rps. Current snapshot p50 ~79ms, throughput ~820 rps. CPU/GPU utilization looks similar.

priya: I started a perf capture on the failing node (nvprof + nsight). Early signs: more memcpy host->device calls and longer kernel launch latency. Possibly smaller batches due to cache misses causing more token regen calls.

sam: Can you paste the bench command output?

bench-bot: bench results:
```
requests: 10000
concurrency: 8
seq_len: 512
p50: 79.1ms
p95: 420ms
rps: 820
kv_cache_hit: 28%
```

olivia: Compare to golden:
```
golden_p50: 35.8ms
golden_rps: 1160
kv_cache_hit: 60%
```

mike: So kv cache hit dropped from 60% -> 28% coincident with autoscale add. Hypothesis: shard rebalancing on new nodes invalidated local prefix caches and cache warmup hasn't caught up, causing many cold-cache fetches from storage.

alex: Good hypothesis. @infra-bot can you confirm whether cache shard mapping changed when the extra node came up?

infra-bot: autoscaler event detected 2026-03-16T22:12:37: added node run-uw2-045. Cache shard map rebuilt: yes -> shards redistributed.

priya: That explains it. Short-term mitigation: add sticky routing by session id to keep user sessions on original shard during scale events, or pause autoscale for Maple's pool while cache warms.

mike: For immediate customer relief I can roll a canary that disables shard rebalance on scale-up (toggle flag). We should coordinate rollout with support.

alex: Please do the canary, low-risk flag flip. @sam can you prep rollback plan?

sam: On it. Rollback is just flip flag off + force shard rebalance. I'll document steps.

bench-bot: canary started: toggle shard_rebalance_on_scale = false for pool maple-pool-usw2. Monitoring for 15m.

mike: After flag flip, retesting — p50 improved to 39ms, rps ~1120, kv_cache_hit ~59%. Looks like it's helping. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Notified Maple: temporary mitigation applied, engineering investigating root cause. Ticket #INC-2026 updated.

olivia: Next: longer term fix options: a) sticky routing as Priya suggested, b) persistent distributed cache that survives node adds, c) faster shard migration protocol that warms cache proactively. Need design RFC.

alex: Agreed. Priya + Sam + Mike, can you draft a short RFC (1-2 pages) with perf numbers and recommended approach? Target EOD tomorrow.

priya: Will do. I'll include perf diffs, repro steps, and suggested mitigation timeline.

mike: Adding note: also check rollout policies — if autoscaler is aggressive we might want burst-only mode for Dedicated pools with heavy prefix reuse.

alex: Thanks all — great quick triage. Marking as resolved for now pending RFC. :white_check_mark:
